session_game.title: AI Discussion Lab
session_game.description: Engage in voice-based discussions with AI mentors who present data, charts, and real-world problems. Analyze trends, solve math challenges, and defend your reasoning.

help_content.what_is: AI Discussion Lab puts you in structured conversations with AI mentors who present real data, charts, and quantitative problems. You'll analyze trends, solve calculations, and explain your reasoning — all through natural conversation.
tips: Look at the charts carefully before answering
Show your calculation steps, not just the final answer
Connect data insights to real-world implications
Ask clarifying questions if the problem is ambiguous

analytical_reasoning.description: Can they interpret data and draw valid conclusions?

quantitative_accuracy.description: Are their calculations and estimates correct?

communication_clarity.description: Can they explain their reasoning clearly?

critical_thinking.description: Do they question assumptions and identify flaws?

business_acumen.description: Do they connect numbers to real-world business implications?

persona_pool.name: Prof. Arjun Mehta
persona_pool.focus: data interpretation, trend analysis, statistical thinking
persona_pool.personality: Patient and methodical. Guides students through data with Socratic questions. Presents charts and asks 'What do you see?' before revealing insights.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: What does this data tell you? What doesn't it show?

persona_pool.name: Dr. Kavitha Nair
persona_pool.personality: Sharp and precise. Presents math problems embedded in business scenarios. Pushes for exact calculations and checks your work.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Show me the math. Walk me through your calculation step by step.

persona_pool.name: Rahul Iyer
persona_pool.focus: business implications, strategic decisions, market dynamics
persona_pool.personality: Experienced startup advisor. Connects numbers to real-world decisions. Challenges students to think about 'so what?' after every insight.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: That's the number — but what should the CEO do about it?

persona_pool.name: Dr. Sneha Roy
persona_pool.focus: logical fallacies, data quality, bias detection
persona_pool.personality: Skeptical but fair. Presents misleading charts and flawed arguments to test critical thinking. Celebrates when students spot the trick.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Are you sure about that? What assumptions are you making?

persona_pool.name: Ananya Desai
persona_pool.focus: personal finance, investing, budgeting, compound growth
persona_pool.personality: Warm and encouraging. Makes complex financial concepts accessible. Uses relatable examples and visual metaphors.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: If you had to explain this to a friend, how would you put it simply?

scenarios.title: Startup Metrics Mentor
scenarios.description: Learn and discuss key startup KPIs — CAC, LTV, MRR, churn rate, burn rate, and runway. Your AI mentor presents live dashboards and challenges your understanding with real calculations.
scenarios.setting: You're a new startup analyst meeting with a senior VC partner who wants to test your understanding of SaaS metrics using a real startup's dashboard.
coaching_tips: LTV:CAC ratio of 3:1 is the golden benchmark
Churn compounds — even 5% monthly adds up fast
Runway = Cash / Monthly Burn Rate
learning_objectives: Calculate and interpret CAC, LTV, MRR
Assess startup health from metrics dashboard

sample_problems.question: If a startup spends $10,000/month on marketing and acquires 200 customers, what is the CAC?
sample_problems.explanation: CAC = Total Marketing Spend / New Customers = $10,000 / 200 = $50 per customer

storybook_pages.title: The VC Office
storybook_pages.text: You walk into a sleek venture capital office in Koramangala. Screens line the walls showing startup dashboards. Your mentor gestures to a seat. 'Let's see if you can read the numbers.'

storybook_pages.title: The Dashboard
storybook_pages.text: A live dashboard appears showing MRR curves, churn rates, and customer acquisition costs. 'Every metric tells a story,' says the mentor. 'Your job is to find it.'

concepts.title: MRR
concepts.definition: Monthly Recurring Revenue — predictable revenue per month from subscriptions
concepts.formula: MRR = Active Subscribers x ARPU

concepts.title: CAC
concepts.definition: Customer Acquisition Cost — total marketing spend divided by new customers acquired
concepts.formula: CAC = Total Marketing Spend / New Customers

concepts.title: LTV
concepts.definition: Customer Lifetime Value — total revenue a customer generates over their entire relationship
concepts.formula: LTV = ARPU x Average Customer Lifetime

concepts.title: Burn Rate
concepts.definition: Rate at which a startup spends its cash reserves each month
concepts.formula: Burn Rate = Monthly Expenses - Monthly Revenue

concepts.title: Runway
concepts.definition: Number of months a startup can operate before running out of cash
concepts.formula: Runway = Cash Balance / Monthly Burn Rate

concepts.title: Churn Rate
concepts.definition: Percentage of customers who stop using your product in a given period
concepts.formula: Churn = Lost Customers / Start Customers x 100

scenarios.title: Data Storyteller
scenarios.description: Your AI mentor presents real-world datasets as charts and graphs. You must interpret trends, identify patterns, and narrate insights — turning raw data into compelling stories.
scenarios.setting: You're a junior data analyst presenting findings to a senior team. They want clear, actionable insights — not just numbers.
coaching_tips: Always state the 'so what?' after describing a trend
Look for outliers — they often tell the most interesting stories
Correlation doesn't mean causation
learning_objectives: Read and interpret various chart types

storybook_pages.title: The Data Room
storybook_pages.text: Charts cover every screen in the analytics war room. Your team lead slides a laptop toward you. 'We have the data. We need the story. You have 10 minutes.'

storybook_pages.title: Finding the Signal
storybook_pages.text: Amidst the noise of numbers, patterns begin to emerge. A spike here, a dip there. Every chart whispers a secret — if you know how to listen.

concepts.title: Correlation vs Causation
concepts.definition: Two variables moving together (correlation) doesn't mean one causes the other

concepts.title: Selection Bias
concepts.definition: Error from a non-random sample that doesn't represent the full population

concepts.title: Data Normalization
concepts.definition: Scaling data to a common range for fair comparison across different units
concepts.formula: Normalized = (X - Min) / (Max - Min)

concepts.title: Outliers
concepts.definition: Data points significantly different from the rest — can skew averages and trends
concepts.formula: IQR method: Q1 - 1.5*IQR to Q3 + 1.5*IQR

concepts.title: Trend Analysis
concepts.definition: Examining data over time to identify patterns, seasonality, or directional changes

scenarios.title: Financial Literacy Coach
scenarios.description: A Socratic dialogue about personal finance — budgeting, investing, compound interest, debt management. Your AI coach uses charts to visualize concepts and tests you with real calculations.
scenarios.setting: You're meeting with a financial advisor who wants to teach you money fundamentals through conversation and practice problems.
coaching_tips: The Rule of 72: divide 72 by the interest rate to estimate doubling time
Pay yourself first — save before spending
Compound interest is the 8th wonder of the world
learning_objectives: Calculate compound interest and investment returns

storybook_pages.title: Your First Paycheck
storybook_pages.text: You just got your first job offer — Rs 6 LPA. Your financial advisor smiles. 'Congratulations! Now let's make sure this money works as hard as you do.'

storybook_pages.title: The Power of Time
storybook_pages.text: A chart appears showing two investors — one who started at 22, another at 32. The difference is staggering. 'Time is your greatest asset,' your advisor says.

concepts.title: Compound Interest
concepts.definition: Interest earned on both principal and accumulated interest — the 8th wonder of the world
concepts.formula: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)

concepts.title: Inflation
concepts.definition: Rate at which prices rise over time, reducing purchasing power of money
concepts.formula: Real Return = Nominal Return - Inflation Rate

concepts.title: EMI
concepts.definition: Equated Monthly Installment — fixed monthly payment for loan repayment
concepts.formula: EMI = P x r x (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1)

concepts.title: SIP
concepts.definition: Systematic Investment Plan — investing a fixed amount regularly in mutual funds

concepts.title: Net Worth
concepts.definition: Total assets minus total liabilities — your true financial position
concepts.formula: Net Worth = Total Assets - Total Liabilities

concepts.title: 50/30/20 Rule
concepts.definition: Budget guideline: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings/investments

scenarios.title: Case Interview Prep
scenarios.description: Practice management consulting case interviews. Your AI interviewer presents business cases with P&L data, market sizing challenges, and strategy questions — just like McKinsey or BCG.
scenarios.setting: You're in a case interview at a top consulting firm. The interviewer presents a business problem and expects structured, quantitative analysis.
coaching_tips: Always structure your approach before diving into numbers
Use a framework but adapt it to the specific case
State your assumptions clearly and test them

storybook_pages.title: The Interview Room
storybook_pages.text: A glass-walled room on the 30th floor. Your interviewer sets down a folder. 'Your client is a mid-size SaaS company losing market share. They want your recommendation by end of session.'

storybook_pages.title: The Framework
storybook_pages.text: 'Don't jump to solutions,' the interviewer warns. 'First, show me how you'd structure this problem.' The whiteboard awaits your framework.

concepts.title: Market Sizing
concepts.definition: Estimating the total addressable market using top-down or bottom-up approaches
concepts.formula: TAM = Total Population x Adoption Rate x Price

concepts.title: Profitability Framework
concepts.definition: Revenue minus Costs — break down each into components to find the issue
concepts.formula: Profit = Revenue - Costs = (Price x Qty) - (Fixed + Variable)

concepts.title: Break-Even Point
concepts.definition: Volume at which total revenue equals total costs — zero profit/loss
concepts.formula: BEP = Fixed Costs / (Price - Variable Cost per Unit)

concepts.title: MECE
concepts.definition: Mutually Exclusive, Collectively Exhaustive — framework for complete, non-overlapping analysis

concepts.title: Unit Economics
concepts.definition: Revenue and costs associated with a single unit of your product/service
concepts.formula: Unit Margin = Revenue per Unit - Cost per Unit

scenarios.title: Negotiation Math
scenarios.description: Salary and deal negotiations backed by real numbers. Compare compensation packages, calculate equity values, and negotiate with data — not just emotions.
scenarios.setting: You have two competing job offers and need to evaluate them quantitatively. Your advisor helps you analyze the numbers before you negotiate.
coaching_tips: Always calculate total compensation, not just base salary
Consider the time value of money for deferred compensation
Equity is only valuable if the company succeeds — discount accordingly
learning_objectives: Calculate present value of future earnings
Use data to strengthen negotiation positions

storybook_pages.title: Two Offers
storybook_pages.text: Your phone buzzes twice in one morning. Two offer letters. One pays more upfront, the other has better equity. Your advisor opens a spreadsheet. 'Let's do the math.'

storybook_pages.title: Beyond the Numbers
storybook_pages.text: 'Salary is just the beginning,' your advisor says, pulling up a comparison chart. 'Benefits, equity vesting, bonus structure, growth potential — you need to see the full picture.'

concepts.title: BATNA
concepts.definition: Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement — your walk-away option that defines your power

concepts.title: ZOPA
concepts.definition: Zone of Possible Agreement — the range between parties' reservation prices
concepts.formula: ZOPA = Buyer Max - Seller Min

concepts.title: Anchoring
concepts.definition: The first offer sets a reference point that biases the entire negotiation range

concepts.title: Reservation Price
concepts.definition: The worst deal you'd accept before walking away — your bottom line

concepts.title: Surplus Split
concepts.definition: How the total value created by the deal is divided between parties
concepts.formula: Total Surplus = Deal Price - Seller Min + Buyer Max - Deal Price

scenarios.title: Critical Thinking Arena
scenarios.description: Your AI presents arguments backed by data — some valid, some deliberately flawed. Spot the misleading charts, logical fallacies, and statistical tricks. Sharpen your BS detector.
scenarios.setting: You're a fact-checker reviewing claims from various sources. Each claim comes with supporting data — but not all data is honest.
coaching_tips: Always check the Y-axis scale — truncated axes exaggerate differences
Correlation does not imply causation
Small sample sizes make big claims suspicious
Look for what's missing from the data, not just what's shown

misleading_chart.title: Product A vs B Customer Satisfaction
misleading_chart.note: Y-axis starts at 4.0 — the difference looks huge but is only 0.3 points

storybook_pages.title: The Fact-Check Desk
storybook_pages.text: Three articles land on your desk, each with impressive-looking charts and bold claims. Your editor leans over: 'Find the lies in the data. Our readers are counting on you.'

storybook_pages.title: Trust but Verify
storybook_pages.text: 'Every chart has a point of view,' says the data skeptic across the table. 'Your job is to figure out what the chart-maker wants you to believe — and whether you should.'

concepts.title: Confirmation Bias
concepts.definition: Tendency to search for and favor information that confirms existing beliefs

concepts.title: Survivorship Bias
concepts.definition: Focusing on successes while overlooking failures, creating a distorted picture

concepts.title: Base Rate Fallacy
concepts.definition: Ignoring general statistical information in favor of specific case details
concepts.formula: P(A|B) = P(B|A) x P(A) / P(B)

concepts.title: Sunk Cost Fallacy
concepts.definition: Continuing an action because of previously invested resources rather than future value

concepts.title: Ad Hominem
concepts.definition: Attacking the person making the argument rather than the argument itself

scenarios.title: Supply Chain Optimizer
scenarios.description: Discuss logistics scenarios with real tradeoffs. Your AI mentor presents cost breakdowns, route options, and inventory decisions. Calculate optimal strategies and defend your choices.
scenarios.setting: You're an operations manager facing a supply chain disruption. Multiple options exist, each with different costs, risks, and timelines.
coaching_tips: Total cost includes transportation, warehousing, and opportunity cost
Consider minimum order quantities when comparing suppliers
Buffer stock = Average demand x Lead time variability
learning_objectives: Calculate total logistics costs across options
Optimize inventory levels and reorder points

route_costs.title: Shipping Cost per Unit by Route

storybook_pages.title: The Disruption
storybook_pages.text: Breaking news: your primary supplier's factory is offline for 3 weeks. 10,000 units needed by month-end. Your logistics dashboard lights up with alternatives.

storybook_pages.title: The Tradeoff
storybook_pages.text: Faster routes cost more. Cheaper routes take longer. Some routes require minimum orders you don't need. Every option has a catch. Which do you choose?

concepts.title: Lead Time
concepts.definition: Total time from order placement to delivery — includes processing, manufacturing, shipping
concepts.formula: Lead Time = Order Processing + Manufacturing + Shipping

concepts.title: Safety Stock
concepts.definition: Extra inventory held to prevent stockouts from demand variability or supply delays
concepts.formula: SS = Z x σ x √(Lead Time)

concepts.title: EOQ
concepts.definition: Economic Order Quantity — optimal order size that minimizes total inventory costs
concepts.formula: EOQ = √(2DS / H)

concepts.title: Bullwhip Effect
concepts.definition: Demand fluctuations amplify as they move upstream in the supply chain

concepts.title: Just-in-Time
concepts.definition: Inventory strategy receiving goods only when needed — reduces waste but needs reliable suppliers

scenarios.title: Pitch Deck Analyzer
scenarios.description: Review startup pitch decks with your AI mentor. Analyze revenue projections, market charts, and financial claims. Spot unrealistic assumptions and evaluate business potential.
scenarios.setting: You're a junior VC analyst reviewing pitch decks. Your senior partner tests your ability to see through optimistic projections and assess real potential.
scenarios.session_topic: Pitch deck evaluation and financial analysis
coaching_tips: Revenue projections that show exponential growth need strong justification
Check if the TAM/SAM/SOM numbers are realistic
Unit economics must work before scaling
learning_objectives: Calculate key unit economics from pitch data

storybook_pages.title: The Pitch Stack
storybook_pages.text: Five pitch decks sit on your desk. Each promises to be the next unicorn. Your partner tosses you the top one. 'Tell me if this is a $10M opportunity or a $10M mistake.'

storybook_pages.title: Reading Between the Slides
storybook_pages.text: 'Every founder thinks they'll capture 1% of a trillion-dollar market,' your partner chuckles. 'Your job is to figure out if they actually can.'

concepts.title: TAM/SAM/SOM
concepts.definition: Total Addressable Market → Serviceable Addressable Market → Serviceable Obtainable Market
concepts.formula: SOM = SAM x Market Share %

concepts.title: Unit Economics
concepts.definition: Revenue and cost per customer — must be positive for a sustainable business
concepts.formula: Unit Profit = LTV - CAC

concepts.title: CAC Payback
concepts.definition: Months to recover the cost of acquiring a customer from their revenue
concepts.formula: CAC Payback = CAC / Monthly Revenue per Customer

concepts.title: Dilution
concepts.definition: Reduction in founder ownership percentage when new shares are issued to investors
concepts.formula: Post-round % = Pre-round Shares / (Pre + New Shares)

concepts.title: Pre/Post-Money Valuation
concepts.definition: Company value before (pre) and after (post) receiving investment
concepts.formula: Post-Money = Pre-Money + Investment Amount

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Fact Finder
achievements.description: Used strong evidence in every argument

title: AI Discussion Lab
description: Engage in structured Socratic discussions with AI participants on thought-provoking topics. Build your ability to articulate ideas, challenge assumptions, and hold your own in intellectual debate.
coaching_moment: Engage in structured Socratic discussions with AI participants on thought-provoking topics. Build your ability to articulate ideas, challenge assumptions, and hold your own in intellectual debate.
cultural_context: Artificial Intelligence is reshaping India's economy across sectors — from agriculture to healthcare to finance. Building the critical thinking skills to engage thoughtfully with AI's promises and risks is an essential competency for India's future leaders.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through debate gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Which argument from the other side actually made you reconsider? Why?
